A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Genome-Factory and retain the same six-module framework and core experiments. The text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Sections 4.1-4.3 report original fine-tuning efficiency measurements, downstream benchmark results, and sparse-autoencoder sequence-length analysis.

after.justification: Sections 3.1-3.3 retain the original experiments and add classical baselines and CTCF-binding analysis. Appendix F reports additional benchmarking and representation-clustering results.

M1.justification: Section 2.3 newly states support for multi-task learning and joint optimization of preprocessing with training; Appendix B explicitly describes multi-task learning as now supported. These extend the reported capabilities, while the six-module architecture, three tuning methods, and core sparse-autoencoder workflow remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds CTCF-binding classification using ENCODE K562 peaks and background sequences, GUANinE sequence-to-function evaluation, and the Genomics Long-Range Benchmark. Appendix F also introduces unsupervised species clustering on retained Genomic Benchmarks data. The original benchmark suites and sequence-length analysis remain.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds six evaluated baselines: CNN, Random Forest, SVM, PWM plus Random Forest, PWM plus linear SVM, and HMM. Appendix F additionally evaluates EVO 2-7B and GROVER. The original six foundation models and three tuning strategies remain in the main comparison.

E3.justification: Original fine-tuning settings are retained. New experiments introduce validation-selected classical baselines, larger-model LoRA evaluation, mean-pooled embeddings with k-means and adjusted Rand index, and logistic probing with latent-zeroing tests. Some new settings are inconsistent: Section 3.2 specifies 4-mer baseline features, whereas Appendix D specifies 6-mers; Table 8's LoRA labeling also conflicts with Table 4.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained sequence-length correlations, Section 3.3 adds a regulatory-feature case study using CTCF-binding prediction and ablates influential SAE units by zeroing their activations. Appendix F adds an unsupervised clustering analysis testing whether embeddings capture species structure. These substantially extend representation analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seeds 14, 28, and 42 and report benchmark means with standard deviations. Additional benchmark rows extend this practice without introducing a different run count, confidence-interval procedure, or significance test. The new probe and clustering results do not document additional uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 3 and all original model scores in Table 4 remain unchanged. V2 adds classical-baseline scores, CTCF accuracy of 0.7881 with latent-zeroing drops of 0.0225, 0.0210, and 0.0196, and Appendix F's larger-model, clustering, GUANinE, and long-range results. Table 8 repeats original full-tuning GUE/GB scores under a LoRA label, preventing interpretation as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations. The added experiments and capability descriptions do not introduce a new formal framework.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains the first integrated framework unifying genomic-model workflows. V2 removes the repeated claim that its Biological Interpreter is the first open-source interpreter, describing it simply as an open-source tool in the abstract and introduction and dropping that priority claim from the conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly limits cross-model rankings to practical comparisons rather than architectural superiority and qualifies the interpreter as an initial step rather than a validated discovery tool. Appendix B adds substantive context-truncation and multi-task-validation limitations. New discussions interpret regulatory and clustering results, while the impact statement identifies concrete deployment risks and prospective safeguards.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds baseline feature construction, validation procedures, hyperparameter searches, and selected configurations. Appendix G supplies detailed CLI commands, configuration fields, file formats, adapter customization, and SAE analysis instructions absent from v1. The advertised repository changes from MAGICS-LAB to WeiminWu2000. These expand documentation without establishing changes to retained experimental settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations covering AlphaGenome, EVO 2, DNABERT-S, newer benchmark suites, and language models. It also withdraws the interpreter's priority claim. Nevertheless, Appendix C largely preserves v1's positioning against fragmented genomic-model tooling and general language-model frameworks; the literature additions do not substantially redefine that positioning.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the document: related work moves from main Section 2 to Appendix C, references precede the appendices, and the front contents page disappears. The title and abstract are revised, explanatory passages are edited throughout, and a structured usage tutorial and new disclosure sections expand the document's organization.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column report to a two-column conference layout with running headers and repositioned displays. Table 4 gains a model-size column and classical-baseline block; new tables present hyperparameters, clustering, and broader benchmarks. Figures 1 and 2 are retained and resized, while the supported-model table is relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Detailed usage guidance, additional comparisons and interpretability analyses, and clearer limits on scientific claims improve usability and calibration over v1. However, new reporting conflicts weaken the empirical expansion: Table 8 labels retained full-tuning scores as LoRA results, and baseline features differ between the main text and Appendix D. The documentation and qualification gains support a limited net improvement, rather than a substantial strengthening of the evidence.
